items.title: Suspect knew intended victim in deliberately set fires in Mississauga: police
items.summary: Police say a woman charged after two fires were deliberately set inside a Mississauga apartment building had been involved in a previous relationship with one of the intended victims. Peel Regional Police acting Det. Sgt. Natosha McBride told reporters Thursday morning one of two people arrested in the arson investigation had a “prior relationship” with a resident of the Lakeshore Road West/Southdown Road building where fires were set in a third-floor hallway on Sept. 20 and again early the following day. Investigators believe the occupants of one unit in particular were deliberately targeted in both fires. However, no significant injuries to residents were reported in either incident, police said, though 18 occupants of the seven-storey Clarkson building were transported to hospital for treatment due to smoke inhalation in the wake of the Sept. m. The second fire also resulted in a large-scale evacuation that displaced a number of residents for an extended time, police added. Also, one police officer who responded to the scene suffered a hand injury that required surgery, Peel police Const. Laurie McCann told the media at Thursday morning’s press conference. The estimated damage as a result of the two blazes was around $1 million. Police charged Joshua Pedersen, 28, left, and Morgan Murphy, 27, centre, in connection with an arson investigation at a Mississauga apartment building. Police are searching for a third suspect, Madison Varga, 30, right.

items.title: 2 arrested, police searching for suspect after Mississauga apartment building allegedly set on fire twice

items.title: Scam targets drivers who use pay-and-display parking machines across Mississauga
items.summary: Mississauga officials are again alerting drivers after more bogus QR code stickers were placed on parking machines across the city in attempts to steal people’s personal and financial information. In a public safety notice issued Thursday morning, the City of Mississauga said officials became aware on Wednesday of fraudulent QR code stickers appearing on pay-and-display parking machines at various locations. “City staff were deployed immediately and removed these stickers from parking machines,” the city said in its notice. Officials issued a similar warning to motorists in April. At that time, the fake QR stickers were placed on dozens of parking machines in Mississauga’s downtown core near city hall. In its latest notice to the public, the city said such unauthorized QR code stickers are “designed to redirect users to third-party payment sites that are not affiliated with the city. ” Mississauga officials added that “QR codes have never been a legitimate method of payment at city parking machines. They will never be placed on parking machines or used to process parking payments.

items.title: Peel Police Charge Two, Still Searching for Third Suspect in Clarkson Apartment Arson Case
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say two people have been charged and a third suspect is wanted after two deliberately set fires at a Clarkson apartment building near Lakeshore Road West and Southdown Road caused an estimated $1 million in damage. According to police, the fires were set in a third-floor hallway on Sunday, Sept. 20, and Monday, Sept. 21, and investigators believe occupants of one unit were deliberately targeted both times. Police said no significant injuries were reported, though the second fire triggered a large-scale evacuation that displaced several residents, and 18 people were taken to hospital for smoke inhalation. Police said they identified three people believed to be involved in the incidents. Joshua Pedersen, 28, of no fixed address, was arrested in Hamilton on Oct. 15 and charged with two counts of arson disregarding human life, two counts of mischief over $5,000, break and enter with intent to commit an indictable offence, and possession of break-in instruments. Morgan Murphy, 27, of Burlington, was arrested on Oct. 26 and charged with two counts each of conspiracy to commit an indictable offence and arson disregarding human life. Both were held in custody pending bail hearings.

items.title: Two charged in arson investigation at Mississauga apartment building; third suspect sought
items.summary: Two people face charges and a third person is sought in an arson investigation at a Mississauga apartment building. Emergency crews responded to fires in a third-floor hallway of an apartment building in the area of Lakeshore Road West and Southdown Road in Clarkson on Sunday, Sept. 20, and Monday, Sept. 21, Peel Regional Police said. Police said the fires were deliberately set in the hallway, and investigators believe the occupants of one unit were deliberately targeted in both fires. No significant injuries were reported in either incident, police said. However, the second fire resulted in a large-scale evacuation that displaced several residents, police added. Police said 18 residents were transported to hospital for treatment of smoke inhalation. The estimated damage is approximately $1 million. Police made two arrests and are searching for an additional suspect in connection with the investigation.

items.title: City Removes Fake QR Code Stickers Found on Mississauga Parking Machines
items.summary: The City of Mississauga says it became aware on Nov. 4 of fraudulent QR code stickers placed on Pay and Display parking machines across the city. According to the city, staff were deployed immediately and removed the stickers, which were designed to redirect users to third-party payment sites not affiliated with the city. The city said scanning and using those codes put residents' personal and financial information at risk. Officials said QR code stickers are never used to collect payment for parking in Mississauga, and that the only legitimate way to pay is through a parking machine's digital payment prompts, which accept coins, payment apps such as Apple Pay or Google Wallet, and major credit cards, with PayByPhone also available in Streetsville. The city said it continues to monitor parking machines and equipment and will respond quickly to any further reports of fraudulent codes.

items.title: Carolyn Parrish Was the Only Candidate to Beat Tedjo in a Single Ward, Certified Results Show
items.summary: Mississauga News says an analysis of certified results from the Oct. 26 municipal election shows mayor-elect Alvin Tedjo won 10 of the city's 11 wards. According to the outlet, outgoing mayor Carolyn Parrish was the only candidate to finish ahead of Tedjo in a ward, winning Ward 5, while former mayor Bonnie Crombie and Coun. Dipika Damerla did not win any ward outright. The analysis found Tedjo's vote share grew in every ward compared to the 2024 byelection. Mississauga News reported that 191,166 people cast a ballot in the election, but 1,212 of them did not vote in the mayoral race, leaving 189,954 total ballots cast for mayor. Tedjo won the race outright with 74,479 votes, according to the certified results.

items.title: Mississauga announces recipient of the 2026 Gordon S. Shipp Memorial Award for Citizen of the Year
items.summary: Ranil Mendis was selected as this year’s recipient after a thoughtful community selection process. The City of Mississauga is pleased to announce that Ranil Mendis was selected as the recipient of the 2026 Gordon S. Shipp Memorial Award for Citizen of the Year. The award was presented to Mendis yesterday evening by Deputy Mayor Matt Mahoney as part of the City’s 2026 annual Civic Recognition awards event. The Citizen of the Year recognizes one Mississauga resident who has given unselfishly for the betterment of their community. Mendis was celebrated for his outstanding leadership, community service and philanthropic efforts, positive attitude and ability to inspire others through co-operation and dedication. Mendis is a long-standing community builder with more than three decades of volunteer service in Mississauga. He has transformed access to youth sport, strengthened community connections and inspired thousands of young people across our city. He arrived in Canada in 1988 and understood early on the barriers that many newcomers face. Drawing on his own experience as an internationally-trained accountant, Mendis has been deeply committed to creating pathways for inclusion, participation and opportunity for others. One of the ways he has done this is through cricket, which he has used as a powerful platform for engagement, belonging and development. He has led initiatives such as the Ontario School’s Cricket Association and the Mayor’s School Cricket Program, which launched in 2013 in collaboration with then-Mayor Hazel McCallion. What began as small, volunteer-led efforts at the school level has grown into structured, City-recognized programming, thanks to Mendis’ collaborative efforts and thoughtful leadership.

items.title: Massive 176,000-Square-Foot Grocery Store Opens in Mississauga with Global Food as Its Draw
items.summary: Food World Plus, described as Ontario's largest grocery store, opened to shoppers on Oct. 30 at 50 Matheson Blvd. East in Mississauga. According to the store, its 176,000-square-foot facility is built around global food, offering products and ingredients from the Mediterranean, Latin America, Europe, Asia, Africa, the Middle East and South Asia. The store said it aims to give shoppers in Mississauga's diverse community access to ingredients they might otherwise need to visit several specialty grocers to find. Beyond its international aisles, Food World Plus is positioning itself as a one-stop destination with a flower section, bakery, deli, fresh meat department and in-house butcher. The store said its meat department includes a dedicated halal section, with meat sourced from a certified halal supplier and handled according to halal standards from delivery through to the cuts prepared for customers. Mayor-elect Alvin Tedjo attended the grand opening alongside Ontario Premier Doug Ford and later welcomed the new store to the city in a social media post.
